promptsSection.title: 💬 Prompts for v0
promptsSection.description: Copy these prompts and paste them into v0 to generate the code for each session:
promptsSection.session1Prompt:
Create a React component called RegenmonDisplay that shows:

1. A Tamagotchi-style container with rounded borders and gradient background
2. A centered pet image (use a placeholder for now)
3. Three progress bars below:
   - Happiness (green color)
   - Energy (blue color)
   - Level (purple color)
4. Each bar should show the percentage with a number
5. An orange button "Create Regenmon" that opens a modal
6. The modal should have:
   - Input for name
   - Selector for type (Fire, Water, Earth)
   - Confirm button

Use Tailwind CSS with modern glassmorphism style. Bars should be animated.
promptsSection.session2Prompt:
Create a ChatInterface component that:

1. Has a scrollable message area
2. Shows chat bubbles:
   - User messages aligned right (orange background)
   - Regenmon messages aligned left (gray background)
3. Input at the bottom with:
   - Text field to write
   - Send button with icon
   - Loading spinner when processing
4. Shows "Writing..." when AI is responding
5. Uses useState to handle messages
6. Includes a button to clear chat

Style: Modern with glassmorphism, smooth animations when messages appear.
promptsSection.session3Prompt:
Create a simple LoginScreen component:

1. Centered welcome screen
2. Game logo or title at top
3. Large "Enter" button that simulates login
4. After login, shows username at top
5. Small "Logout" button in top right corner
6. Uses localStorage to remember if user logged in

Style: Minimalist and clean, uses orange and gray colors.
promptsSection.session4Prompt:
Create an EvolutionSystem component:

1. Shows current Regenmon stage:
   - Baby (level 1-5)
   - Young (level 6-10)
   - Adult (level 11+)
2. Progress bar to next evolution
3. Daily missions section:
   - List of 3 missions
   - Checkbox to complete
   - Coin reward
4. "Upload Photo" button that opens:
   - Drop area to drag image
   - Image preview
   - "Evaluate" button that simulates AI
5. Shows earned coins with animation

Style: Cards with glassmorphism, modern icons.
promptsSection.session5Prompt:
Create a SocialHub component:

1. User pets gallery:
   - Grid of cards with photo, name and level
   - Clicking shows details
2. Rankings table:
   - Top 10 users by coins
   - Avatar, name, coins, position
3. Button to interact with another pet
4. Marketplace section:
   - Grid of items (food, accessories)
   - Price in coins
   - Buy button

Style: Professional, use tabs to separate sections, smooth animations.

glossary.title: Quick Glossary for Vibecoders
glossary.subtitle: All technical terms explained in simple language. Search for any word you don't understand.
glossary.searchPlaceholder: Search for a term... (e.g., API, Deploy, State)
glossary.noResults: No terms found matching your search.

deploy.definition: Upload your app to the internet so it runs 24/7. Like publishing a video on YouTube: you go from having it only on your computer to everyone being able to see it.

production.definition: Your app running on the internet, accessible to everyone. It's the "final mode" after you finish building and testing.

localhost.definition: Your app running only on your computer (nobody else can see it). Like a private rehearsal before the show.

url.definition: Web address of your app (e.g., myapp.vercel.app). Like a house address on the internet.

framework.definition: Predefined tools and rules to build apps faster. Like a LEGO box with instructions vs building from scratch.

bug.definition: Something that doesn't work as it should in your app. Like a hole in a net: you need to find it and fix it.

localStorage.definition: Memory in your browser (deleted if you clear cookies). Like sticky notes: temporary and only in your browser.

database.definition: Memory on the internet (permanent, not deleted). Like a giant Excel file that lives in the cloud: always there.

api.definition: Bridge that connects your app with external services (like AI, images, payments). Like a waiter: you order, they bring what you need.

apiKey.definition: Special password to use AI services or APIs. Like your house key: without it you can't get in.

endpoint.definition: Specific address where your app requests or sends information. Like different windows at a bank: one for deposits, another for withdrawals.

json.definition: Format for organizing information that apps understand. Like speaking the same language between different programs.

prompt.definition: Instructions you give to the AI. The clearer they are, the better the responses.

context.definition: What the AI remembers from previous conversations. Like short-term memory: it's lost if you spend too much time.

multimodal.definition: AI that understands text + images at the same time. Like a teacher who can read your essay AND see your drawings.

temperature.definition: How creative the AI is (0=precise and repetitive, 1=creative and unpredictable). Like the radio volume.

token.definition: Unit of text that AI processes (≈4 characters). Like counting words, but more technical. More tokens = more expensive.

systemPrompt.definition: Base personality of the AI. You tell it "you're a motivational coach" and it will always respond that way.

ui.definition: Everything you see on screen: buttons, text, colors, images. It's your app's "face".

component.definition: A reusable piece of your interface (e.g., button, card, menu). Like LEGO pieces you can combine.

state.definition: Information that changes in your app (e.g., happiness level, coins, name). It's your interface's "active memory".

props.definition: Information you pass from one component to another. Like giving specific instructions to each piece.

responsive.definition: Your app looks good on mobile, tablet and computer. It automatically adapts to screen size.

auth.definition: Login system that verifies who you are. Like showing your ID at the entrance.

session.definition: The time you're logged into the app. When you log out, it ends.

authToken.definition: Temporary pass that proves you've already logged in. The app saves it so it doesn't ask for your password every time.

permissions.definition: What you can and can't do in the app based on your user type (admin, normal user, visitor).

session1Troubleshooting.title: Common Errors - Session 1
session1Troubleshooting.subtitle: If something isn't working, here are solutions to the most frequent problems.

error1.title: "My Regenmon doesn't appear on screen"
error1.description: You created your pet but nothing shows, just a blank screen.
solutions: 1. Verify the name has at least 3 letters
2. Check that you've selected a type (Fire/Water/Plant)
3. Open browser console (F12) and look for errors in red
4. Refresh the page (F5) and try again
error1.why: Your app expects certain information before showing the Regenmon. If something is missing (name, type, image), it doesn't know what to show and stays blank.

error2.title: "Page doesn't load after deploy"
error2.description: You deployed to Vercel but the link shows 404 error or infinite loading.
solutions: 1. Wait 2-3 minutes - Vercel takes time to process
2. Refresh the page several times (Ctrl + F5)
3. Open the link in incognito window to avoid cache
4. Check in your Vercel dashboard that deploy says "Ready"
error2.why: Vercel needs time to build your app, upload it to servers and distribute it globally. It's not instant, but once ready it works 24/7.

error3.title: "My Regenmon disappears when I reload the page"
error3.description: You create your pet but when you reload (F5) everything starts over.
solutions: 1. Ask v0: "Add persistence to save the Regenmon"
2. Verify that v0 added code to remember data
3. Reload the page and create your Regenmon again
4. If it still doesn't work, tell v0: "The Regenmon doesn't save on reload"
error3.why: Your app needs a place to "remember" your Regenmon's information. Without that permanent memory, when you reload the page everything is forgotten and starts from scratch.

error4.title: "Build in v0 fails with errors"
error4.description: When you try to deploy, v0 shows red errors and doesn't compile.
solutions: 1. Read the error message calmly - it usually says what's missing
2. Look for common errors: undefined variables, missing imports
3. Ask v0 to "fix the build errors"
4. If it doesn't work, describe the specific error to v0
error4.why: Build errors are the code telling you "I'm missing something to work". It could be a variable, an import, or incomplete code.

needHelp.title: Still stuck?
needHelp.description: If none of these solutions worked:
steps: Copy the exact error you see
Go to Discord and paste the error in #help
Share your v0 link so someone can see the code
While waiting for response, try starting fresh with a clean project

session2Troubleshooting.title: Common Errors - Session 2
session2Troubleshooting.subtitle: Frequent problems when integrating conversational AI and their solutions.

error1.title: "Error: Invalid or non-working API Key"
error1.description: You added your API Key but the app says it's invalid or fails to connect.
solutions: 1. Verify you copied the complete API Key without extra spaces
2. Check in your AI provider account that the key is active
3. If you have no credits, the API won't work (check balance)
4. Generate a new API Key if the previous one doesn't work
error1.why: The API Key is your password to use the AI. If it has errors, is expired, or you have no credits, the provider rejects the connection.

error2.title: "Chat doesn't respond at all"
error2.description: You write messages but the Regenmon doesn't answer, just infinite loading.
solutions: 1. Open console (F12) and check for errors in red
2. Verify the API Key is configured correctly
3. Confirm your internet connection works
4. Check for rate limits (too many requests too fast)
5. Wait 30 seconds and try again
error2.why: Your app sends the message to the AI on the internet, waits for response, and displays it. If something fails in that process (API, connection, code), it keeps waiting.

error3.title: "Chat history gets deleted on reload"
error3.description: You chat with your Regenmon but when reloading (F5) the entire conversation disappears.
solutions: 1. Verify the code saves messages in localStorage
2. Open F12 → Application → Local Storage and look for the history
3. Ask v0 to add chat persistence
4. Confirm each message is saved after sending it
error3.why: Without localStorage, messages only exist in temporary memory. When reloading, that memory is cleared and you lose all the history.

error4.title: "Regenmon responds with weird or off-context things"
error4.description: The AI responds but doesn't have the right personality or says nonsense.
solutions: 1. Review the system prompt - it must define clear personality
2. Include Regenmon type information (Fire/Water/Plant)
3. Add current stats (happiness, energy) to the prompt
4. Define clear boundaries: "Respond as a pet, not as an assistant"
error4.why: The AI responds according to the instructions it receives. If the prompt is vague or lacks context, responses will be generic or inconsistent.

error5.title: "Error: Insufficient credits or limit reached"
error5.description: The app was working but now says there are no credits or you reached the limit.
solutions: 1. Check your balance in the AI provider console
2. Optimize the prompt to use fewer tokens
error5.why: Each message to the AI costs tokens (credits). Providers usually give free credits to start, but they eventually run out if you use the API a lot.

needHelp.title: Still having problems?
needHelp.intro: For AI debugging, include this information:
steps: Screenshot of the exact error (console F12 included)
Your API Key (only first 10 characters: sk-ant-api03...)
The system prompt you're using
Contact: brian@frutero.club

session3Troubleshooting.title: Common Errors - Session 3
session3Troubleshooting.subtitle: Solutions for authentication, data, and resource system problems.

error1.title: "Login doesn't work or fails constantly"
error1.description: You try to login but it shows error or doesn't let you in.
solutions: 1. Verify the login service is properly connected
2. Try with incognito window to start fresh
3. Ask v0 to review the login configuration
error1.why: The login system needs to be properly configured to work. If something isn't connected correctly, it won't let you in.

error2.title: "Coins don't save or disappear"
error2.description: You earn coins but when reloading they go back to zero or are lost.
solutions: 1. Confirm you use database (Supabase) not just localStorage
2. Verify each gain/expense updates the database
3. Check Supabase logs to see if queries work
4. Confirm userId is correctly linked
error2.why: localStorage is temporary. For real persistence you need database. If you don't save in DB or there are query errors, data is lost.

needHelp.title: Database problems?
steps: Screenshot of Supabase logs (don't include keys)
Description of what should happen vs what actually happens
Your table structure (schema)
Contact: brian@frutero.club

session4Troubleshooting.title: Common Errors - Session 4
session4Troubleshooting.subtitle: Solutions for problems with multimodal AI, image evaluation, and progress.

error1.title: "AI can't see/analyze images"
error1.description: You upload images but AI responds as if it doesn't see them.
solutions: 1. Confirm you're using claude-3-opus/sonnet (not claude-2)
2. Verify the image converts to base64 correctly
3. Check the format is image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp
4. Confirm image size doesn't exceed 5MB
error1.why: Only Claude 3 (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) can see images. Claude 2 is text-only. The image must be in correct format and proper size.

error2.title: "Progress doesn't save or goes back to zero"
error2.description: You train your Regenmon but when reloading the progress disappears.
solutions: 1. Make sure to save in database not just state
2. Update DB after each successful training
3. Verify the experience/level field exists in your table
4. Confirm update queries work (Supabase logs)
error2.why: Progress must be in permanent DB. If you only update React state, it's lost when reloading the page.

error3.title: "Visual evolution doesn't change"
error3.description: Your Regenmon levels up but the image stays the same.
solutions: 1. Verify you have different image URLs per stage
2. Confirm the logic correctly detects level/stage
3. Check the component re-renders with the new image
4. Use state/props to control which image is shown
error3.why: Visual evolution is simply showing different images based on level. If the logic doesn't update the URL or the component doesn't re-render, it stays the same.

needHelp.title: Problems with multimodal AI?
steps: Claude model you're using (claude-3-opus-20240229)
Format and size of the image you upload
Exact error message from the API
Contact: brian@frutero.club

session5Troubleshooting.title: Common Errors - Session 5
session5Troubleshooting.subtitle: Solutions for problems with social features, public profiles, and interactions.

error1.title: "Public profiles don't show or display 404 error"
error1.description: You try to view a public profile but it doesn't load or shows page not found.
solutions: 1. Verify the dynamic route is configured (/profile/:userId)
2. Confirm RLS policies allow public profile reading
3. Check the query brings data for the correct user
4. Make sure an "is_public" or similar field exists in the table
error1.why: Public profiles need dynamic routes and proper database permissions. If RLS blocks public reading, no one can see profiles.

error2.title: "Notifications don't appear"
error2.description: Interactions happen but notifications aren't generated.
solutions: 1. Confirm each interaction creates a record in notifications table
2. Verify the recipient's userId is correct
3. Check the notifications component queries the DB
4. Make sure there's a polling system or real-time subscriptions
error2.why: Notifications are DB records shown to the destination user. If they're not created, there's nothing to show.

error3.title: "Feed doesn't show other Regenmons"
error3.description: There are users but the feed appears empty or only shows yours.
solutions: 1. Verify the query DOESN'T filter by userId (must bring all)
2. Confirm RLS allows public reading of public Regenmons
3. Check there's an "is_public: true" field in the records
4. Make sure to exclude your own Regenmon from the feed (optional)
error3.why: The feed must bring records from ALL users (except current). If you filter by userId or RLS blocks, you'll only see yours.

intro.p1: In this first session, you'll take the most important step of the entire bootcamp: creating your first real digital product, even if you've never programmed before.
intro.p2: This isn't about memorizing code or understanding complex concepts. It's about learning to build with the help of artificial intelligence, step by step, seeing immediate results.
intro.p3: By the end of this session, your Regenmon will exist, will be alive in an app, and you'll be able to access it from any device.

whatYouWillLearn.title: What will you learn in this session?
whatYouWillLearn.subtitle: During this session you'll learn the foundations that all modern applications use, but explained in a simple and practical way.

items.title: 1. Programming with AI assistance
items.description: You'll learn what it means to develop with AI: not writing code from scratch, but explaining what you want to build and improving the result little by little.
items.subtitle: You'll see how to:
list: Give clear instructions to the AI
Adjust until it looks and works as you expect
items.footer: This process of ask → review → improve will be a key skill throughout the bootcamp.

items.title: 2. What is a component and why it matters
items.p1: You'll learn about components (reusable pieces of your interface), which are the parts that make up an app.
items.p2: You don't need complex theory: you'll just understand that an app is built in parts (like blocks) and that each part has a clear function.
items.p3: Your Regenmon will be one of those components.

items.title: 3. Saving information (so it doesn't get lost)
items.description: You'll learn how an app remembers things, even when you close the browser or reload the page.
items.subtitle: In this session:
items.footer1: will be saved so they don't disappear.
items.footer2: This introduces you to the concept of state (information that changes in your app) and persistence (saving data permanently), something fundamental in any real application.

items.title: 4. Publishing your app on the internet
items.description: You won't just create something that works on your computer.
items.subtitle: In this session you'll learn to:
list: Connect your project to a deploy platform (upload your app to the internet)
Publish your app automatically in production (running 24/7 on the internet)
items.footer: This means your Regenmon isn't an exercise, it's a product accessible on the internet.

whatYouWillDo.title: What will you do during the session?
whatYouWillDo.subtitle: Throughout the session, step by step, you will:
list: Create the initial project of your app with AI help
Design the main screen where your Regenmon lives
Create a flow where: the user gives it a name, chooses its type, brings the Regenmon to life
Display visually: the name, the sprite, its stats
Save that information so it doesn't get lost
Publish the app and verify it works on mobile and computer
whatYouWillDo.footer: You'll do all this seeing results in real time, without needing prior knowledge.

whatYouWillAchieve.title: What are you expected to achieve at the end?
whatYouWillAchieve.subtitle: By finishing this session you should have:
list: A deployed app with a public URL
Information that persists when reloading the page
A solid foundation for the following sessions

important.message: The confidence that you can create software, even if you've never done it before.

whyImportant.title: Why this session is important
whyImportant.intro: This session breaks the biggest barrier of all:
whyImportant.outro: After today, that idea ceases to exist. From here on, everything we do will be to improve, expand, and connect what you've already created.

bridge.title: Preparing the next step
bridge.intro: So far your Regenmon is visual (it has a face, stats, buttons). In the next session you'll give it a brain (conversational AI).
bridge.needsTitle: What do you need before Session 2?
needs: A Claude API Key (like a password to use AI)
Understand that the AI isn't in your app, it's on the internet (that's why you need the "key")
Know that every time your Regenmon "talks", it asks Claude for help
bridge.analogy: 💡 Analogy: Imagine your Regenmon is a ventriloquist's dummy. In Session 1 you built the dummy. In Session 2 you'll give it a voice (Claude is the ventriloquist).

intro.p1: In the previous session you gave life to your Regenmon. Now it has a name, type, sprite, and stats. It exists. But it doesn't do anything yet.
intro.p2: In this session you'll give it the most important capability of all: speech.
intro.p3: Here you'll learn how to connect an artificial intelligence model to your app so the Regenmon responds to messages, reacts to what you say, and begins to feel real.
intro.p4: By the end of this session, you'll have a Regenmon that interacts with you in real time, responding according to its personality and remembering what you tell it.

whatYouWillLearn.title: What will you learn in this session?
whatYouWillLearn.subtitle: This session is where the digital becomes personal. You'll learn to connect conversational AI to your app and structure an interaction that feels real and coherent.

items.title: 1. What is a conversational AI model (and how to use it)
items.p1: You don't need to be an AI engineer to use AI.
items.p2: Here you'll understand what a language model is (like ChatGPT or Claude) and how to connect it to your app by sending requests and receiving responses.
items.subtitle: You'll learn to:
list: Connect your app to an external AI model
Send the user's message and receive the model's response
Display the response in the interface clearly
items.footer: This introduces you to the concept of API (gateway that connects your app with external services) and external services, something that's in absolutely all current applications.

items.title: 2. How to give your Regenmon personality (basic prompt design)
items.p1: It's not enough to connect the AI. You must tell it how to behave.
items.p2: Here you'll discover the concept of system prompt (instructions that define the AI's personality): the internal instructions you give the model so it responds in a certain way.
items.subtitle: You'll design:
list: How the Regenmon speaks (tone, style, personality)
How it reacts according to its type (Water, Earth, Fire)
What it knows about itself (name, stats, history)
items.footer: This is your first experience with prompt engineering, one of the most important skills in AI development.

items.title: 3. How to display a conversation (chat interface)
items.description: Creating the text bubble isn't the challenge. The challenge is structuring the message flow clearly.
items.subtitle: You'll implement:
list: An input where the user types
Loading states while the model responds
items.footer: This is your introduction to user experience (UX) design in interactive applications.

items.title: 4. Chat memory (so the Regenmon remembers what you told it)
items.p1: If it forgets everything every time you talk to it, there's no real conversation.
items.p2: Here you'll learn to maintain the chat history and send it to the model, so the responses have context (what the AI remembers from previous conversations).
items.subtitle: You'll implement:
list: Send conversation context to the model
Save the history so it doesn't get lost on reload
items.footer: This introduces you to the concepts of state management and conversational context.

whatYouWillDo.title: What will you do during the session?
whatYouWillDo.subtitle: Step by step, you'll implement:
list: Connect your app to a language model (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, etc.)
Create a system prompt that gives the Regenmon personality
Design a chat interface with input, message bubbles, and scroll
Display loading states while the model responds
Save the chat history to maintain context
Make the Regenmon respond according to its type and stats
Verify everything works locally and in production
whatYouWillDo.footer: You'll do all this with the same methodology: ask the AI for help, iterate, test, and adjust.

whatYouWillAchieve.title: What are you expected to achieve at the end?
whatYouWillAchieve.subtitle: By finishing this session you should have:
list: A functional chat where you can write to your Regenmon
Conversation history that doesn't get lost on reload
A clear and fluid conversation experience
The feeling that your Regenmon is real

important.message: Understanding that integrating AI into an app isn't magic, it's just sending and receiving messages in a structured way.

whyImportant.title: Why this session is important
whyImportant.intro: This session shows you something fundamental:
whyImportant.quote: "AI isn't magical, it's a tool you can control"
whyImportant.outro: After today, you'll know how to make any app talk, respond, and behave intelligently. And that completely changes the type of products you can build.

bridge.title: 🎭 What's next: Identity
bridge.intro: Your Regenmon already speaks, but doesn't recognize you. Every time you reload the page, it's like you're a stranger.
bridge.subtitle: In Session 3 you'll learn:
list: How to make your Regenmon know who you are (login)
The difference between YOUR pet and other users' pets

bridge.title: 📈 What's coming: Progress
bridge.intro: Your Regenmon already knows who you are and stores your information. Now it needs to grow and evolve based on how you care for it.
bridge.subtitle: In Session 4 you'll implement:
list: AI that evaluates images (not just text)
bridge.analogy: 💡 Analogy: Your Regenmon now has identity and resources. In Session 4 it will learn to grow like a Tamagotchi would: leveling up, changing form, and responding to your consistent care.

session4.title: 🌱 Session 4 — Your Regenmon Evolves
session4.subtitle: When your actions leave a mark and your creation grows with you

intro.p1: In this session an important change occurs in your Regenmon's story:
intro.p2: It no longer just reacts to what you do, now it grows because of it.
intro.p3: Here you'll learn how an application can evaluate real actions, provide feedback, and show progress over time. It's the point where your app starts to reflect habits, consistency, and evolution.

whatYouWillLearn.subtitle: In this session you'll focus on evaluation, progress, and evolution, three key concepts in modern products that seek to motivate and accompany the user.

whyImportant.outro: You learn how to design systems that motivate, accompany, and show real progress, a very valuable skill in modern digital products.

bridge.title: 🌍 The final step: Community
bridge.intro: Your Regenmon works perfectly... but it's alone. In the last session you'll transform your project into a social experience.

session5.subtitle: When your creation stops being alone and becomes part of a community
